negative_findings.description: No public, machine-readable register of designated critical infrastructure objects in the banking/financial sector was located. NBU Resolution No.69/2025 and Regulation No.178/2022 define criteria for designation, but the resulting list appears to be restricted-access.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the criteria documents surfaced; no register endpoint or downloadable list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without the register, one cannot tell which banks/PSPs are inside the heavier SSSCIP-linked compliance perimeter, which is the key segmentation variable for compliance-driven demand.

negative_findings.description: CERT-UA/SSSCIP financial-sector threat products are frequently TLP-marked and circulated to constituents rather than published; the public site shows aggregate statistics and TLP:CLEAR reports only.
negative_findings.result_summary: Public artefacts found were TLP:CLEAR analytics and news; sector-specific advisories to banks were not publicly enumerable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The most operationally specific requirements reach banks through closed CSIRT channels, so open-source monitoring will systematically lag the real compliance signal.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetch-verified. Several are known to be bot-defended or paywalled (ligazakon, lexology) and zakon.rada.gov.ua often rate-limits automated clients.
negative_findings.result_summary: All URLs recorded from search-result metadata; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A 403 from these hosts must be read as bot defence, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: The acronym 'НБУ' collides with Незалежна асоціація банків України ('НАБУ', also the anti-corruption bureau NABU) in Ukrainian search results, and 'кіберзахист' vs 'кібербезпека' vs 'інформаційна безпека' are used inconsistently across SSSCIP and NBU acts.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries needed disambiguating co-terms (постанова Правління, Держспецзв'язку) to avoid anti-corruption-bureau noise.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection keyed on these acronyms will pull large volumes of irrelevant material.

brief: Ukraine's cyber/infosec rulebook for banks and PSPs is written by two disjoint authorities that must be tracked in parallel: the NBU (Regulations No.95/2017 and No.178/2022, updated by No.69/2025 on financial-sector critical infrastructure and No.143/2025 for non-bank financial service providers, with a reported end-2026 compliance horizon and a DORA-alignment framing), and SSSCIP/Держспецзв'язку together with CERT-UA, whose authority now flows from Law No.4336-IX of March 2025 and CMU Resolution No.712/2025 on security profiles and security authorisation. Operationally, CSIRT-NBU (cyber.bank.gov.ua) is the highest-value single source because it carries both the 72-hour incident-reporting duty and sector guidance, while bank.gov.ua's legislation and news pages give the earliest sight of drafts and consultation windows. The data-protection strand is separate again and currently supervised by the Verkhovna Rada Ombudsman, with GDPR-style reform pending as bill 8153 — track the Rada bill card for stage changes rather than commentary. The main blind spots are the non-public register of designated critical infrastructure objects and the not-yet-published financial-sector sectoral security profile, both of which would sharpen who is in scope and by when.
